CANON-DATALIFECYCLE-001 — Data Lifecycle, Erasure, Redaction & Immutable Ledger Reconciliation Authority: CONST-DATA-001, CONST-DATA-003, CONST-PRIV-001, CONST-CONSENT-001, TECH- LEDGER-001 Purpose Resolves the tension between borrower privacy rights, portability, deletion or erasure requests, retention obligations, and immutable audit ledger requirements. Core Rule. The platform may preserve immutable audit lineage while minimizing, redacting, tombstoning, tokenizing, or cryptographically destroying personal data where legally required and operationally permissible. Required Controls 1. Distinguish business records, audit records, regulated records, borrower-provided records, derived records, and public-source records. 2. Apply retention schedules by data class, jurisdiction, and regulatory basis. 3. Erasure requests must be evaluated against legal hold, audit, regulatory, and contractual retention requirements. 4. Immutable ledger entries may not be deleted, but sensitive payloads must be minimized, encrypted, tokenized, or replaced with tombstone references where appropriate. 5. Redaction must preserve replay context without exposing unnecessary personal data. 6. Cryptographic destruction may be used where deletion is required but audit shell preservation is necessary. 7. Portability exports must exclude unrelated third-party, lender, security, or privileged information. 8. All lifecycle changes must be recorded as canonical events. The governance runtime must enforce delegation boundaries, quorum requirements, escalation thresholds, and capacity monitoring — not merely document them. Constitutional authority: HUMAN-GOV-001 (Vol I §3.36). Every governance decision is a governed event (CANON-EVENT-001, Vol III §3.49) and must be logged with full actor, authority, and authorization context. This architecture directly implements the Facilitation Doctrine (FACILITATION-001): human governance saturation controls ensure that human oversight remains substantive — Furlong facilitates governance; it does not replace it. ● DELEGATION CHAIN ENFORCEMENT: Delegation Registry documents all active chains. Validation: chain max 3 levels; delegating actor authorized for role; delegation period active; delegated actor accepted. Invalid delegation → rejected and logged as Tier B event. ● QUORUM ENFORCEMENT: Constitutional-tier: two-thirds Governance Board must authenticate and confirm. Regulatory-tier: minimum 3 human confirmations. Operational-tier: role-based authority matrices. Quorum checks enforced at middleware layer — architectural bypasses not possible. ● EMERGENCY DELEGATION ACTIVATION: When State 3 (EMERGENCY) or 4 (CONTINUITY) active → runtime reads succession plan, activates secondary governance actors within 30 minutes, logs succession as Tier A event, sets 72-hour expiry on emergency delegation authority. ● COMMITTEE ESCALATION ENFORCEMENT: Runtime monitors for: (1) multi-tier impact, (2) governance precedent, (3) dissenting annotations, (4) constitutional conflict. Each trigger routes decision to Governance Board escalation queue. ● ESCALATION BATCHING CONTROLS: Batch size limited to decisions reviewable within scheduled period. The governance runtime must enforce delegation boundaries, quorum requirements, escalation thresholds, and capacity monitoring — not merely document them. Constitutional authority: HUMAN-GOV-001 (Vol I §3.36). Every governance decision is a governed event (CANON-EVENT-001, Vol III §3.49) and must be logged with full actor, authority, and authorization context. This architecture directly implements the Facilitation Doctrine (FACILITATION-001): human governance saturation controls ensure that human oversight remains substantive — Furlong facilitates governance; it does not replace it. ● DELEGATION CHAIN ENFORCEMENT: Delegation Registry documents all active chains. Validation: chain max 3 levels; delegating actor authorized for role; delegation period active; delegated actor accepted. Invalid delegation → rejected and logged as Tier B event. ● QUORUM ENFORCEMENT: Constitutional-tier: two-thirds Governance Board must authenticate and confirm. Regulatory-tier: minimum 3 human confirmations. Operational-tier: role-based authority matrices. Quorum checks enforced at middleware layer — architectural bypasses not possible. ● EMERGENCY DELEGATION ACTIVATION: When State 3 (EMERGENCY) or 4 (CONTINUITY) active → runtime reads succession plan, activates secondary governance actors within 30 minutes, logs succession as Tier A event, sets 72-hour expiry on emergency delegation authority. ● COMMITTEE ESCALATION ENFORCEMENT: Runtime monitors for: (1) multi-tier impact, (2) governance precedent, (3) dissenting annotations, (4) constitutional conflict. Governance becomes institutionally valid only when traceable to operational enforcement, audit evidence, replay evidence, and certification verification. Core Rule. Governance shall not exist solely as policy, aspiration, or declared intent. Governance maturity evolves through Defined → Implemented → Auditable → Replayable → Certified → Institutionalized. This doctrine reserves constitutional authority for Volume VII — the Unified Governance Conformance Matrix. Required Controls 1. Every doctrine must trace to a runtime guard, database artifact(s), audit event(s), replay evidence, and a certification status. 2. Certification status uses defined stages (Not Started, Planned, In Progress, Partial, Complete, Certified). 3. Phased onboarding: doctrines enter the UGCM on a published onboarding schedule. A doctrine not yet onboarded remains fully governed under its home volume and is not deemed non-conformant solely for awaiting UGCM onboarding; it is classified 'UGCM-pending' with a target onboarding date. 4. A doctrine that has been onboarded to the UGCM and cannot then be traced to enforcement, audit, replay, and certification is non-conformant until remediated. 5. The 'Certified' stage requires independent verification by a party outside the doctrine's implementation team (internal independent reviewer or external auditor); the verifier and cadence are recorded in Volume VII. Section 3.51 — Human-in-the-Loop Governance Architecture HITL-GOV-001 — Human-in-the-Loop Governance Architecture Human oversight is constitutional accountability infrastructure. Privacy governance is constitutional data sovereignty infrastructure — consent, deletion, and portability rights must remain replay-preserved, explainably enforceable, and borrower-transparent. IMPLEMENTATION REQUIREMENTS Implement append-only storage: use a managed service with append-only policy enforced at the storage layer (e.g., AWS S3 Object Lock, Azure WORM storage) or a purpose-built ledger database. SHA-256 hash chain: each ledger entry contains hash(prior_entry_content + current_entry_content). On write, compute and store chain_hash alongside event payload. Nightly hash-chain verification job: traverse chain from genesis to latest, verify each link. Alert within 15 minutes of any chain break. Ledger entry schema: {event_id, event_type, entity_id, actor_id, timestamp_utc, payload_hash, chain_hash, schema_version}. Retention: 7 years. All entries queryable by event_type, entity_id, actor_id, and timestamp range within 5 seconds for up to 10M entries. RECOMMENDATION Implement a separate Ledger Integrity Monitor service with its own access credentials — the monitor should not share service account with any write path to prevent a single compromised credential from both corrupting and masking corruption.
